set.body:
The 2026-09-08 repair qualification implements and independently verifies PM/DL with explicit z or modified Knapp-Hartung inference, but declines admission of a universal small-sample default. In 20,000 null studies with n=8, known unequal sampling variances 0.04..1 and true tau2=.2, DL/z rejects 11.475%, DL/mKH 6.595%, PM/mKH 6.895% at alpha=.05. No failed fits. With n=80, three regressors and independently estimated first-level variances (df=8), PM/mKH rejects 8.10% when tau2=0. These are statistical calibration failures, not implementation-parity failures.

Owner: ScalaFIM group inference and first-level uncertainty provenance; generic resampling primitives belong in Multivar. The new GroupModel.mixedEffects requires explicit estimator and inference choices; compatibility DL/z remains named. Evidence: docs/verification/group-repair-2026-09-08.md and tools/group-repair/jvm/GroupRepairCalibration.scala. Existing qualification ticket bd-01M20NE80H1DXKQCFQZT15FTTP can finish with this documented decline; this ticket owns the next method admission, separately from estimator expansion bd-01KX2CQZGWBQ3KKX7BWE28X3T2 and file-backed execution bd-01KX6G9BFJRERNFRWR17WT0YGN.

Scope: compare justified nuisance-aware parametric/studentized wild/bootstrap or alternative adjusted methods for explicitly admitted independent-subject designs, retaining first-level SE/df provenance where required. An intercept-only exact symmetry method may be a bounded first admission; it must not imply covariate/repeated-measure validity. Do not choose a method or tune a threshold solely to this calibration seed.

Acceptance: predeclare estimand, independence/exchangeability, variance assumptions, inference target and fallback/refusal boundaries; independent reference and fresh held-out null/power calibration covering small n, unequal precision, nuisance covariates, estimated SEs and heterogeneity boundaries; interval coverage and failure availability; JVM/JS numerics and completed-work CPU/allocation evidence; only then enable a calibrated default in a consumer. Pointwise validity and spatial FWER/FDR claims remain distinct. No automatic universal default is admitted by the current repair.
set.title: Admit calibrated group inference for unequal and estimated subject variances
